AUTH-001.description: Create a monorepo (or three coordinated repos) for AuthN, AuthZ, and User Info with shared CI/CD pipelines, branch protection, and code-owner rules.
acceptance: Repository created with clear top-level directories: services/authn, services/authz, services/userinfo, specs/, infra/, docs/
CI runs on every PR: lint, test, build artefact
Branch protection requires PR review and passing CI before merge
Code-owners file maps each service directory to its named owner
Secrets management for CI is via the chosen secrets store, not committed config
AUTH-001.spec: Monorepo recommended for the worked example because it keeps the spec files, infra, and code together. Three separate repos are valid if organisational policy demands service ownership boundaries. CI must run from the same source-of-truth checkout that holds the OpenAPI and AsyncAPI specs so that contract verification has access to them.

AUTH-002.description: Stand up a KMS (or HSM-backed equivalent) with three logically isolated key namespaces: AuthN signing, AuthN credential encryption, User Info PII encryption.
acceptance: KMS instance reachable from each service's deployment environment
Three key namespaces created with distinct IAM access policies
JWT signing keypair generated (RS256 or ES256) with rotation cadence configured
Credential encryption KEK created with annual rotation cadence
Profile PII encryption KEK created in a logically separate namespace
AUTH-002.spec: Reference: auth-separation_pci-compliance_v1.md section 3 (key rotation table). Reference: auth-separation_database-spec_v1.md section 5.4 (column encryption). The AuthN MFA secret KEK and the User Info PII KEK live in separate KMS namespaces so a compromise of one does not extend to the other.

AUTH-003.description: Issue and distribute service identity certificates so that AuthN, AuthZ, User Info, and the bus authenticate each other with mTLS.
acceptance: Internal CA issuing service certificates with 90-day validity
Each service has a unique identity certificate
Bus broker has a certificate that publishers verify
Cert rotation automated and tested
Revocation procedure documented in runbook
AUTH-003.spec: Reference: auth-separation_architecture_v1.md section 1 (trust boundaries). Use the platform's native mesh (Istio, Linkerd, Cilium, Consul) or a lightweight per-service identity tool such as SPIFFE/SPIRE. Hand-rolled mTLS works but adds operational overhead; not recommended.

AUTH-004.description: Deploy the message bus (Kafka, NATS, RabbitMQ, or equivalent) with the four channels declared in the AsyncAPI spec.
acceptance: Channels created: user.lifecycle, authn.events, authz.events, userinfo.events
Publisher authentication via mTLS certificate
Retention policy configured per channel
Dead-letter handling configured
Bus accessible from all three service environments
AUTH-004.spec: Reference: specs/auth-separation_events_v1.yaml (channels list). Choose the broker based on the deployment environment. Configure at-least-once delivery as the floor; exactly-once via transactional producers is preferred for the audit and lifecycle channels.

AUTH-005.description: Deploy logs, metrics, and distributed tracing infrastructure with conventions that all three services will follow.
acceptance: Log forwarder with structured JSON logs ingested into central store
Metrics scraping with Prometheus-compatible format
Tracing backend with OpenTelemetry collector
Per-service dashboards templated
Logs do not contain raw credentials, raw tokens, or unmasked personal data
AUTH-005.spec: Reference: auth-separation_gdpr-compliance_v1.md section 8 (logging constraints). Reference: auth-separation_pci-compliance_v1.md section 2 Requirement 10 (logging). Tracing is mandatory because any production request crosses two or three service boundaries.

AUTH-006.description: Add Spectral and openapi-spec-validator to CI to gate any change to the OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specs.
acceptance: Spectral runs on every PR that touches specs/*.yaml
openapi-spec-validator confirms 3.1 conformance
AsyncAPI CLI validates the events file
House style ruleset catches missing examples and vague descriptions
Broken specs block merge
AUTH-006.spec: Reference: spec-formats_openapi_v1.md section 5 (linting). Reference: spec-formats_asyncapi_v1.md section 6 (linting). Treat broken specs the same as broken builds.

AUTH-010.description: Stand up the credential store with encryption at rest, restricted access, and 35-day point-in-time recovery.
acceptance: Database instance deployed with KMS-backed encryption at rest
Application user has DML only; migration user has DDL
Backup with 35-day PITR enabled
Restore tested in pre-production
Network access restricted to the AuthN service identity
AUTH-010.spec: Reference: auth-separation_database-spec_v1.md sections 2 and 8. Choice of storage product is open; capability list applies. A row store with strong consistency and unique-constraint enforcement is the typical fit.

AUTH-011.description: Apply the four-entity schema (Users, MFA Factors, Refresh Tokens, Recovery Codes) with the indexes specified in the database spec.
acceptance: All four tables/collections created with the columns and types in the spec
Six indexes created and verified
Unique constraint enforced on login_identifier (case-folded)
Migration scripts version-controlled and reversible
Schema applied to non-production environments by CI/CD
AUTH-011.spec: Reference: auth-separation_database-spec_v1.md section 2.1 (schemas) and 2.2 (indexes). Use the forwards-and-backwards-compatible migration pattern from section 6.4.

AUTH-012.description: Stand up the AuthZ store with encryption at rest and sub-millisecond read latency for the assignments-by-user query.
acceptance: Database instance deployed with KMS-backed encryption at rest
Hot-path read latency benchmarked at sub-1ms p99
Backup with 35-day PITR enabled
Restore tested
Network access restricted to the AuthZ service identity
AUTH-012.spec: Reference: auth-separation_database-spec_v1.md sections 3 and 8. Strong consistency on writes is required: an assignment must be visible to the next decision check.

AUTH-013.description: Apply the five-entity schema (Permissions, Roles, Role Permissions, Role Assignments, Policies) with the indexes specified.
acceptance: All five tables/collections created
Indexes including assignments_user_idx, assignments_idem_unique created
Foreign key relationships enforced
Migration scripts reversible

AUTH-014.description: Provision the append-only audit log store with high write throughput and forwarding to immutable storage.
acceptance: Append-only enforcement at the storage layer
Write throughput benchmarked above expected peak
Forwarding pipeline to immutable object storage configured
Hash chain integrity field present in schema
Online retention 12 months, cold tier 36 months
AUTH-014.spec: Reference: auth-separation_database-spec_v1.md section 4. Reference: auth-separation_soc2-compliance_v1.md AZ-AUD controls.

AUTH-015.description: Stand up the profile store with column-level encryption support, encryption at rest, and PITR.
acceptance: Database instance deployed with KMS-backed encryption at rest
Column-level encryption support verified for binary columns
Backup with 35-day PITR enabled
Network access restricted to the User Info service identity
PII KMS key wired in

AUTH-016.description: Apply the four-entity schema (Profiles, Preferences, Consent Grants, Audit Shell) with column-level encryption on PII fields.
acceptance: All four tables created
PII columns stored as ciphertext with KEK identifier
Indexes created per spec
Audit Shell schema present and empty
Migration reversible
AUTH-016.spec: Reference: auth-separation_database-spec_v1.md section 5. Reference: auth-separation_gdpr-compliance_v1.md section 4 (controller obligations).

AUTH-020.description: Run the chosen OpenAPI generator against specs/auth-separation_authn-api_v1.yaml to produce a server stub in the target language.
acceptance: Stub compiles and serves all endpoints (returning 501 Not Implemented at first)
Generated DTOs match the OpenAPI components.schemas exactly
Generator config committed; regeneration is one command
No hand-edits to generated files
CI runs a test step and produces a build artefact for this stub (inherited from AUTH-001 acceptance criterion 2, deferred here by owner decision 2026-08-15)
AUTH-020.spec: Reference: spec-formats_openapi_v1.md section 5 (code generation). Stack decided in ADR-0006: C# / .NET 9 with ASP.NET Core, generated by NSwag (openapi2cscontroller, /ControllerStyle:Abstract, /UseActionResultType:true). Note kiota generates clients only and cannot produce a server stub. The contract is immutable; if the stub is wrong, fix the spec, do not edit the stub.

AUTH-021.description: Run the OpenAPI generator against specs/auth-separation_authz-api_v1.yaml to produce the AuthZ server stub.
acceptance: Stub compiles and serves all endpoints
Generated DTOs match the spec
Regeneration scripted

AUTH-022.description: Run the OpenAPI generator against specs/auth-separation_userinfo-api_v1.yaml to produce the User Info server stub.
acceptance: Stub compiles and serves all endpoints
Generated DTOs match the spec
Regeneration scripted

AUTH-023.description: Use AsyncAPI Generator (or Modelina) to produce typed publishers and consumers for the four channels.
acceptance: Publisher classes generated for AuthN, AuthZ, User Info
Consumer scaffolding generated where needed
CloudEvents envelope serialisation correct
Schema validation on publish enabled
AUTH-023.spec: Reference: spec-formats_asyncapi_v1.md section 6 (code generation). Reference: specs/auth-separation_events_v1.yaml.

AUTH-030.description: Implement POST /users: validate input, hash password with KDF, persist user, publish UserRegistered event.
acceptance: POST /users returns 201 with user_id on success
Returns 409 on duplicate login_identifier
Returns 422 on validation failure
Password hashed with Argon2id (or scrypt/bcrypt) at agreed cost factor
UserRegistered event published within 2 seconds
AUTH-030.spec: Reference: specs/auth-separation_authn-api_v1.yaml POST /users. Reference: features/auth-separation_acceptance-registration-and-first-login_v1.feature 'Successful registration' scenario.

AUTH-031.description: Implement POST /sessions: verify credentials, issue access and refresh tokens, publish UserAuthenticated or AuthenticationFailed.
acceptance: Returns 200 with TokenPair on success
Returns 401 on bad credentials, with AuthenticationFailed event
Returns 403 with MfaChallenge if MFA enrolled
Access token signed with the JWT signing key
Refresh token persisted as SHA-256 hash, plaintext returned to client only
AUTH-031.spec: Reference: specs/auth-separation_authn-api_v1.yaml POST /sessions. Access token must contain no role or permission claims (architecture document section 3).

AUTH-032.description: Implement GET /.well-known/jwks.json publishing the current public verification keys.
acceptance: Returns the active public key(s) in JWKS format
Includes the previous key during rotation window
Response cached at the edge with appropriate max-age
Endpoint accessible without authentication
AUTH-032.spec: Reference: specs/auth-separation_authn-api_v1.yaml GET /.well-known/jwks.json. The JWKS URL is the trust anchor for every downstream service that verifies tokens.

AUTH-033.description: Implement POST /sessions/refresh with single-use rotation: consume old token, issue new pair, mark old token used.
acceptance: Returns 200 with new TokenPair on valid refresh token
Returns 401 if refresh token is invalid, expired, or already used
Old refresh token marked as used atomically with new token issuance
Replay of the old token is rejected
Password change verifies current password before accepting new one
All other sessions revoked on successful change
Reset initiation returns 202 regardless of identifier existence (no enumeration)
Reset confirmation accepts a single-use token within its TTL
TOTP enrolment returns secret and otpauth URL
Verify endpoint accepts a current code and activates the factor
Challenge endpoint accepts a code matched against the challenge_id
MFA secrets stored as ciphertext under the credential KEK

AUTH-036.description: Implement POST /decisions/check and POST /decisions/batch with sub-10ms p99 latency.
acceptance: Returns DecisionResponse with allowed, decided_at, optional reason and matched_rule
Default to deny on missing roles or unknown actions
Latency benchmarked at sub-10ms p99 under expected load
Decision is deterministic for fixed inputs
AUTH-036.spec: Reference: specs/auth-separation_authz-api_v1.yaml /decisions endpoints. Reference: auth-separation_soc2-compliance_v1.md AZ-DEC controls.

AUTH-037.description: Implement role definitions, role-permission mapping, and assignment endpoints with idempotency support.
acceptance: Roles can be created, replaced, deleted
Role assignments respect Idempotency-Key on retried requests
RoleAssigned and RoleRevoked events published on every change
expires_at honoured: expired assignments treated as revoked at decision time

AUTH-038.description: Implement policy create/list endpoints and the evaluation engine that resolves allow/deny with conditions.
acceptance: Policies can be created and listed
Effect resolution (allow/deny precedence) documented and tested
Condition evaluation sandboxed
PolicyChanged event published on every change

AUTH-039.description: Write one audit entry per decision with prev_hash and entry_hash; expose via GET /audit/decisions.
acceptance: Every decision produces exactly one audit entry
Hash chain validated by background job hourly
GET /audit/decisions paginated and filterable by user_id and date range
Append-only enforcement at storage layer
AUTH-039.spec: Reference: auth-separation_database-spec_v1.md section 4. Reference: auth-separation_soc2-compliance_v1.md AZ-AUD controls.

AUTH-040.description: Implement GET /users/me, PATCH /users/me, GET /users/{userId} with AuthZ check.
acceptance: Self read returns the caller's profile fields
PATCH updates only specified fields
Other-user read calls AuthZ for user.read permission and returns 403 if denied
ProfileUpdated event lists fields_changed (names only, no values)
GET returns current preferences
PUT replaces preferences atomically
PreferencesUpdated event published

AUTH-042.description: Implement consent grant list, create, withdraw with version capture and evidence.
acceptance: List returns active grants
Grant records key, version, granted_at, evidence
Withdraw sets withdrawn_at and emits ConsentWithdrawn event
Per-key withdrawal is independent of other grants

AUTH-043.description: Implement POST /users/me/export with asynchronous delivery of a structured export.
acceptance: Returns 202 with request_id
Export contains every personal field, preferences, consent history, audit metadata
Delivery mechanism (signed URL via email) implemented
Statutory one-month SLO with internal seven-day target

AUTH-044.description: Implement DELETE /users/me to publish UserDeletionRequested and scrub PII asynchronously.
acceptance: Returns 202 with request_id
UserDeletionRequested event published
PII columns scrubbed within 60 seconds
Audit shell row created with request_id and timestamps

AUTH-050.description: Build a reusable middleware that verifies access tokens against the JWKS endpoint for use by AuthZ, User Info, and resource APIs.
acceptance: Verifies signature, issuer, audience, expiry
Caches JWKS with reasonable TTL
Rejects tokens with unknown kid as unauthenticated
Used by AuthZ, User Info, and at least one example resource API
AUTH-050.spec: Reference: auth-separation_architecture_v1.md section 3 (token model). Verification is local against JWKS; introspection (POST /sessions/introspect) is a fallback for resource servers that prefer remote validation.

AUTH-051.description: Each service publishes its events and consumes the events it cares about. Add CloudEvents envelope wrapping and signature verification.
acceptance: Each service publishes its own events with CloudEvents envelope
Publisher signs payloads with its mTLS identity certificate
Consumer verifies signatures on receipt
Schema validation on publish and consume
AUTH-051.spec: Reference: specs/auth-separation_events_v1.yaml. Reference: spec-formats_asyncapi_v1.md sections 3 and 10.

AUTH-052.description: Add a read-through cache for the assignments-by-user query; invalidate on RoleAssigned/RoleRevoked/PolicyChanged events.
acceptance: Cache hit ratio measurable
Invalidation triggered within seconds of relevant event
TTL set short enough that event loss does not let stale data survive more than minutes
Cache miss path benchmarked separately

AUTH-053.description: On UserDeletionRequested, each service performs its scrub and emits a per-service confirmation; a coordinator publishes UserDeleted when all three are done.
acceptance: AuthN revokes sessions, deletes credentials and MFA secrets
AuthZ removes all role assignments
User Info scrubs PII columns, retains audit shell
UserDeleted published listing all three services within 60 seconds
Acceptance scenario 'Account deletion propagates across all three services' passes

AUTH-060.description: Script and dry-run rotation for JWT signing keys, credential KEK, profile PII KEK, mTLS certs, backup keys.
acceptance: Each key has a documented rotation cadence
Rotation scripts tested in pre-production
Emergency rotation procedure documented and rehearsed
JWKS includes both old and new keys during the rotation window

AUTH-061.description: Document and rehearse the breach response sequence for credential compromise, PII exposure, and policy misconfiguration.
acceptance: Three runbooks: PCI-style for AuthN, GDPR for User Info, SOC 2 for AuthZ
Each runbook covers contain, investigate, rotate, notify, report, postmortem
Tabletop exercise scheduled in the next 90 days
AUTH-061.spec: Reference: auth-separation_pci-compliance_v1.md section 4. Reference: auth-separation_gdpr-compliance_v1.md section 6. Reference: auth-separation_soc2-compliance_v1.md CC7.

AUTH-062.description: Forward every decision audit entry to immutable object storage within seconds of write.
acceptance: Forwarding pipeline running with monitored lag
Object storage configured as write-once
Online store loss recoverable from immutable copy
Pipeline stall alerted as P2 incident

AUTH-063.description: Generate a quarterly report comparing the on-call rotation against accounts with production access; flag drift.
acceptance: Report generated automatically each quarter
Owner named for each flagged drift item
Closure tracked in incident system

AUTH-070.description: Wire the scenarios in features/ (seven files, 21 scenarios) to a Cucumber-compatible runner and run end-to-end against a deployed stack.
acceptance: A BeforeAll-style hook asserts the full stack is ready before any scenario runs -- AuthN, AuthZ and User Info responding, and the event bus up with consumers connected -- rather than repeating those steps as a Background in each feature file (AS-06)
Every scenario in every file under features/ passes against a running stack (21 scenarios across 7 files)
Suite runs in CI on every release candidate
Failures block release
AUTH-070.spec: Reference: features/ -- seven feature files, 21 scenarios, one Feature per file. features/README.md states the suite-wide readiness precondition the hook must assert; no feature file carries a Background.

AUTH-071.description: Run Schemathesis (or Dredd) against each service's deployed instance to detect contract drift.
acceptance: Contract verification suite runs in CI for each service
Failures block deployment
Stateful tests cover authentication and pagination

AUTH-072.description: Run a CI consumer that subscribes to the bus during the acceptance run and validates every observed payload against the AsyncAPI schemas.
acceptance: CI consumer running against test bus
Schema violations cause acceptance run to fail
Includes envelope and per-event payload validation

AUTH-073.description: Simulate a login storm at 2x expected peak; confirm AuthN remains responsive and credential database absorbs writes.
acceptance: Login p99 latency under 500ms at 2x peak
No errors at sustained peak for 1 hour
Credential database CPU and IO within bounds

AUTH-074.description: Drive sustained load against POST /decisions/check; confirm sub-10ms p99.
acceptance: Decision p99 latency under 10ms at 2x peak
Cache hit ratio measured
No errors for 1-hour soak

AUTH-075.description: Engage a qualified vendor for a black-box and authenticated penetration test of all three services.
acceptance: Test report received
All critical and high findings closed before launch
Medium and low findings tracked with owners

acceptance: All three services deployed per the chosen topology
Conformance items 1 to 4 from the topology doc met
Rollback procedure tested

AUTH-081.description: Deploy each service across at least two availability zones behind a load balancer.
acceptance: Each service has at least two replicas in different zones
Load balancer health checks configured
Zone failure simulated successfully

AUTH-082.description: Document and rehearse disaster recovery for each store, including cross-service consistency on restore.
acceptance: Per-store DR runbook written
Annual drill scheduled and first drill executed
RTO and RPO targets met during drill
AUTH-082.spec: Reference: auth-separation_soc2-compliance_v1.md A1.3. Reference: auth-separation_database-spec_v1.md sections 2.6, 3.7, 5.6.

AUTH-083.description: Walk through every conformance checklist (README, three compliance docs, deployment topology, database spec) and capture sign-off.
acceptance: Each conformance item has an evidence reference
Outstanding gaps tracked with owners
Sign-off recorded by security committee
AUTH-083.spec: Reference: every '_v1.md' conformance checklist in this folder.

acceptance: Smoke suite passes in production
